At the same time, the evolution of the production by activity sectors was determined, this allowing the knowledge of the sectors from each country that contribute to the achievement of the gross domestic product and of the economic well-being.

articleTitle: Allocation of Economic Parameters Between Heat and Electricity for a CHP
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The paper presents a new and innovative method for the allocation of economic parameters between heat and electricity production for energy modelling of a combined heat and power plant (CHP). Combined heat and power plants for heat supply considered in this study are for: District Heating (DH) consumers (DH cogeneration); industrial consumers (industrial cogeneration) and; district and industrial consumers (mix cogeneration). According to the consumer’s heat energy demand, the CHP deliver mainly hot water and steam. The technologies considered for CHP cogeneration are: 1) Steam boilers running on fossil fuel, wood, wood waste, urban solid wastes, etc. connected with steam turbines (back pressure turbine, condensing turbine with adjustable bleedings or back pressure turbine with adjustable bleedings); 2) Gas turbines running on natural gas, distillate, etc. equipped with heat recovery; 3) Combined cycle gas turbine on natural gas, distillate etc. with cogeneration steam turbines.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Fractional-Slot Concentrated-Wound Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Redundancy for Critical Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: nowadays, lots of critical applications use electric motor drives that require a high degree of redundancy, in various industrial areas, such as automotive, aerospace, military, nuclear power plants and many other. This paper presents a finite element analysis on a fractional-slot concentrated-wound permanent magnet synchronous motor with double feed three-phase delta-connected winding used in automotive electric steering systems, with different coils distributions. For this application, redundancy is imposed by safety reasons. Different fault scenarios are considered.

articleTitle: A New Gain Matrix of the Luenberger Observer for the Vector Control Systems with Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This article presents a new gain matrix of the Luenberger observer determined based on the parallel mathematical model of the induction motor with iron loss. The Luenberger observer estimates the stator current and rotor flux of an induction motor. The testing of the proposed observer is done both in the open loop and in the closed loop of a vector control system. All tests are performed by simulation in Simulink.

articleTitle: Arc protection function modelling using Petri nets
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper presents the modelling of the arc protection function, ANSI 50ARC, using Petri Nets inference logic (PN). Then, using the simplified model of the protection system, a model for arc fault diagnosis in a complex installation is proposed. For exemplification, the model is built for a simple MV/LV substation. The input information for the PN model can come directly from the field devices (circuit breakers and protection relays) or from a SCADA System. The model can be used to detect quick and precise the location of the fault in case of normal operation of the protection element (circuit breakers and protection relays) or malfunctions of these devices.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Active Damping Techniques in Electric and Hybrid Electric Powertrains
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Hybrid electric powertrains have a limited power source on board which can interact with the traction drives at the certain wheel power and traction force. As the traction drive normally realizes the commanded torque, the DC-link can become unstable and oscillate until it reaches the protection triggering level. There are several basic techniques for handling this problem by adjusting the control system of the traction drive. All of them affect the dynamic speed-torque characteristics of the drive in different ways decreasing its the performance as well. This paper considers the methods of proportional power regulation, proportional torque regulation. A new method of DC-link current negative feedback is proposed in this paper. The simulation was carried out to compare these techniques. The simulation results have shown that the most promising is the control strategy with DC-link current negative feedback, which shows ease of tuning and good damping capability.

articleTitle: Obtaining of the Paints with Electromagnetic Shielding Properties
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility issues and the generated because of this interference are a major concern on electrical and electronic products, mainly in the domains of communications, information technology, transportation, safety and medical services. This paper presents the obtaining process of nano-structured paints and primers with electromagnetic shielding properties, designed for automotive components sector.

articleTitle: Study on the possibilities of detecting recyclable waste using the dielectric properties of materials
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The present paper is presenting a study on the possibilities of sorting recycling wastes by using the dielectric properties of the materials they are realized with the purpose of using for an automatic sorting system. Daily we produce a lot of waste coming from our food, drinks, cosmetics, goods, etc. A part of the packages are using the same material, but other are using various combinations of materials, stacked in layers or side by side pieces. Usual recycling packages contain plastic, paper, glass, metal. These materials have different dielectric properties, different textures and different specific weight. The toughest problem is to separate paper and plastic, due to their similar weight and dielectric properties. The present study presents some measurements of various recycling packages on their electric permittivity while being tested as dielectric in a capacitive sensor. Results of the measurements and discussions are presented in the paper together with some useful conclusions.

articleTitle: Practical Application for Monitoring the Behavior of a Series RLC Circuit
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Monitoring the behavior of an RLC series circuit is very important. Under certain conditions, the quality factor of the circuit may indicate that over voltages may occur at the terminals of the circuit elements (inductor and capacitor). The phenomenon of over voltages can be desired or unwanted. It would be desirable if it is needed, when aiming the amplification of the supply voltage of the circuit. If the over voltage occurs accidentally it can additionally charge the capacitor. Using this practical application, students can visualize the conditions under which over voltages can occur, and can additionally check the obtained practical results. Also, this paper aims to support the students which have deficiencies in understanding of the details related to the phasor representation of electrical signals in the sinusoidal steady state. Practically, through the phasor representation of voltage and current signals, the students will be able to monitor the evolution of the phase difference between these two signals for different values of the inductance, the capacitance and the working frequency.

articleTitle: PLCs’ Inputs and Outputs Response Time Testing Application
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: In general terms, a programmable logic controller (PLC) is a computer that by one side includes a microprocessor, but on the other side does not have any monitor, or keyboard, or mouse. It is developed especially to endure very severe industrial environments. A PLC is frequently used in civil applications such as washing machines, traffic signals controlling systems or elevators. The PLCs are very useful in different industries to control and monitor various production processes, as well as numerous building systems. Due to the fact that PLCs are used in real-time processes, it is very important to prepare the students to understand all the aspects of PLC’s utilization in practice. Thus, it is quite significant for the students to know how to test the response time regularly for PLCs inputs and outputs. This paper presents an application that can be used for determination of the response time of PLCs that are used to perform the laboratory classes of the discipline that deals with the study of PLCs.

articleTitle: Power Quality Requirements for Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper focus on the analysis on compatibility between power grid quality voltage and integration of PV systems. In this paper, the voltage harmonic distortion is calculated at the bus bars of the test network and it is evaluated the suitability between PV plant and bus bars of the grid where the PV system would be connected.

articleTitle: Exergetic Approach for Magnetic Refrigeration
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The paper presents an exergetic analysis of a magnetic regenerator in the current context of artificial cold production. Methods for calculating the exergetic balance for a group of physical processes were presented as component parts of integral processes. If we examine the heat transfer process and contemplate the calculation formulas of entropy generation and exergy losses, we see that in this case, the situation is much clearer than the mass exchange process. In the second case, the results obtained give the possibility to make only some qualitative comparisons. In technological processes we can find a much richer range of cases in which the specifics of energy and exergetic are not yet clear to the end. And, of course, the first and second principles of thermodynamics should be applied to their study. The results acquired after modeling in MatLab environment allow obtaining a numerical model of a magnetic regenerator performed on the principle of parallel gadolinium plates, operating at room temperature.

articleTitle: Development and Testing of Different Types of Polymer-based Electrical Actuators
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Engineering of smart materials is just beginning and the already existing results confirms the possibility of using smart materials in interesting directions. This paper presents multiple results after development and testing of different types of polymer-based actuators, as the fields and applications in which intelligent materials are currently and may further be used are numerous, such as micromotors, robotics, medicine (surgery – artificial organs and filters, orthopedics – implants, ophthalmology) as well as aerospace applications.

articleTitle: A Deeper Analysis about the Impact of Prosumers on Power Losses in Low Voltage Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The pressure of climate change and the need for the adoption of renewable sources have led to a strong development of technology within microgrids (μG). The modular and scalable nature presents opportunities for the development of a new class of users in μG (i.e. the prosumers). The large-scale integration of small-scale renewable energy sources (SSRES) creates challenges for today's classic electricity distribution networks. The paper proposes a simulation method for optimal integration of prosumers to minimize active power losses in μG. For a deeper analysis regarding the influence of the prosumers on the μG power losses, 24 hour real load consumption and generation profiles are used. The study's findings show that a more effective μG operation by the optimal allocation of the PV panels on the μG can decrease the active power losses up to 35% in a day.

articleTitle: Vertical Axis Wind Turbines: Open Airfoils and Plastic Blades
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The paper addresses two aspects of vertical axis wind turbines. In the first part, aerodynamic aspects were addressed. Two types of blade segments were tested in the wind tunnel, both defined by the NACA 0018 airfoil. One of the two blades had an opening of 1/3 of the chord length at the trailing edge. The results showed that the airfoil’s performance, in terms of lift/drag ratio, was not strongly affected by the opening. However, when applied for vertical axis wind turbines, the open blades (J blades) developed a higher productivity than the turbine with normal blades.The second part addresses the possibility of manufacturing small wind rotor blades (1.5 m) from HDPE plastic. The process consisted of three main steps: shredding the plastic, obtaining a plastic sheet through hot pressing, cold pressing the hot plastic sheet into a specially prepared mold. A blade segment was manufactured this way in order to prove the possibility. After this, a structural analysis was performed on a 1.5 m helical open blade. The simulations showed that this material could be a viable solution for small vertical axis wind turbines.

articleTitle: Application of S7-1200 PLC for Temperature Monitoring of a Railway Separator
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Measuring temperature in various systems can be quite challenging, such as in power breakers, railway power lines contacts or in electric traction substations. This article presents an on-line monitoring system with Human Machine Interface to supervise the temperature of a high railway voltage separator. The temperature is measured using an infrared temperature sensor that converts the temperature in an electrical signal, which, afterwards, is used as an analogue input for the Siemens S7-1200 PLC.

articleTitle: Extending Sensor Type Connections to a PLC
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Increasing the number of smart home installations, in conjunction with the development of Internet of Things (IoT) systems, are part of the solution needed to reduce carbon dioxide emissions that are accused of having led to significant climate change in recent years. Developing a smart home implies distributing several types of sensors for collecting data relevant to a smart, optimized and safe operation. Many smart houses use a PLC as the control system with controls and sensors connected to inputs, acquired data being used to elaborate output signals needed to drive execution units. In this paper, we propose a method to connect to PLCs different intelligent sensors allowing the extension of data types that can be collected and used in the PLC-based system. The method is based on the capacity of many PLCs to communicate via TCP/IP protocol.

articleTitle: On the Transient of the Induction Machine with Rotor in Motion when Connecting to the Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: In this paper the transient stator currents and torque of the induction machine have been evaluated in the case of the machine connected to the power supply when the rotor is moving. The study is based on the comparison between the transient determined by the linearization of the mathematical model and the regime determined on the basis of the nonlinear model. Since the nonlinear model cannot be used analytically, the comparison has been carried out only by simulation. The main transient parameters are taken into account, namely the peak values and the time interval for which the errors are reasonable.

articleTitle: About Communication Networks Used within Electrical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: In the paper are presented some comparative aspects of communication networks used in substation regarding electrical equipment. The current communication methods found within the electrical equipment are presented. On last part of the paper, are highlight the advantages and disadvantages of the current communication methods used within electrical equipment. The communication networks are various and suitable for particular cases. In the paper it was argued the choice of a certain type of communication used for monitoring electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Acceptance Testing of the Six-Phase Asynchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper addresses to the issue of program organization and testing attempts to accept with 6 phases machines, a less researched field. According to the standards, several tests, in particular those of experimental definition of the parameters, it must be performed at a sinusoidal supply voltage, which imposes the need to develop and manufacture new test equipment, involving substantial costs. The paper argues for a way to perform tests that require sinusoidal voltage supply, by transforming the six-phase asynchronous machine (with an even number of three-phase systems) by simple procedures for reconnecting the phase windings, in a symmetrical three-phase. This allows tests to be performed in no-load operation, with load and short-circuit mode, using the standard equipment of three-phase electrical machine testing laboratories. This eliminates the need for new multiphase sinusoidal power supply equipment.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Long-term Optimal Scheduling of Photovoltaic Panels Cleaning
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: One of the major problems facing photovoltaic (PV) farms in the Middle East is dust accumulation. Whether it is through a sandstorm or other climate-related variables, dust negatively impacts solar panel performance. Consequently, there is a greater need for cleaning to mitigate the issue of dust on solar panels. Currently, there are numerous cleaning technologies that have been implemented around the world. However, as water is a scarce resource in the Middle East, cleaning is costly in both labor and resources. Therefore, it is important to optimally schedule the solar panel cleaning while using minimal resources. This paper introduces a new method for optimal long-term scheduling for PV panel cleaning. The proposed method relies on developing virtual scenarios for dust accumulation and using these scenarios to find the optimal schedule for the cleaning. Simulation results on a typical PV farm show a significant reduction in the operational cost using the proposed approach versus a fixed cleaning schedule.

articleTitle: The Assessment of Human Exposure in Iasi-City using Data Provided by The National Autonomous RF-EMF Monitoring System throughout 2020
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: In the last decades, we are all witnessed to an explosive increase and development of applications that integrate the electromagnetic environment in our day-by-day life. The principal and delicate problem of the human exposure to a various types of electromagnetic field (EMF) sources is very challenging and up to date one, being considered to have a higher level of importance especially from the safety point of view. The population has always been reluctant and ambiguous about the introduction of new technologies, like the actual case of the implementation around the world of the new 5G NR mobile communications technology for example. For that, the responsible authorities from different countries must conduct studies to ensure and to track the fact that the exposure at new technology is safe or not. So, that being said, the process of monitoring the EMF produce by a diversity of different sources of radiofrequency electromagnetic fields (RF-EMFs) should be a priority in our days. In the study presented in this paper, using the National Autonomous Broadband EMF Monitoring System, a continuous 24/365(hours/days) monitoring system, we analyze real-time monitoring data for all months of the year 2020 for all EMF monitoring fixed station installed at that time in Iasi-city giving a special attention for the last month of the year, December 2020. It was made also an analysis and comparison off the measured data with those imposed by international organizations and national regulatory bodies. At the final a set of preliminary conclusions have been taken.

articleTitle: Influence of the Prosumers on the Replacement Strategies of the Aged Transformers from the Electric Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The impact of the prosumers on the replacement strategies of the transformers from the electric distribution networks imposed by the Eco-design Directive of the European Commission is studied in the paper. Thus, an original decision-making methodology, integrating two stages, is proposed considering various penetration degrees of the prosumers. In the first stage, the "importance" classes of aged transformer replacement are identified following a clustering process. An optimization model, having as objectives the maximization of the energy-saving and post-payback period, was used to determine the optimal solution associated with the rated power of the transformers from each class. The obtained results demonstrated the efficiency of the proposed methodology for a transformer fleet with 20 units belonging to a Romanian Distribution Network Operator.

articleTitle: Islanded Microgrids control by using Grid Former and Synthetic Slack Bus concept - A preliminary analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Microgrids are entities which will become more frequent in areas with high penetration of renewable energy sources. Therefore, there is an increasing need for reliable tools appropriate for load-flow and dynamic analysis, especially for the off-grid operation. However, simulation compatibility for on-grid operation must be also available. Furthermore, microgrids are by their nature weak: some loads may be comparable with generation units, which are also divided into grid former and grid followers. In this paper, a preliminary assessment of such microgrids is made, based on load-flow analysis on a Quasi-Steady Static Time Series and a Synthetic Slack Bus concept. These are used to obtain realistic results and appropriate deployment solutions for independent microgrids operation.

articleTitle: Increasing System Flexibility through a Combination of Pumped-Hydro and Battery-Storage Systems. An Overview of Possible Developments
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The task of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> neutrality in 2050 with high targets for 2030 ask for a large deployment of Renewable Energy Sources. However, the volatility of RES asks also for a high flexibility in the system, to be provided with a high share of storage resources. Traditional Pumped Hydro Powerplants (PHP) and newer Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are competing technologies which need to co-participate to this effort. The paper is analyzing a combination of these resources, with the purpose to be able to cover the need of flexibility, by giving also a preliminary view for Republic of Moldova. The analysis is using the strengths of each technology, and investigates appropriate business models and opportunities for BESS, to highlight that they have many opportunities to be exploited in a future high-RES scenario. It is shown that these options are able to have a complementarity which brings synergies and provide meaningful solutions for the high need of storage in an decarbonized energy paradigm.

articleTitle: Solution for remote microclimate monitoring in Low Voltage / High Voltage switchgear cells
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: In this paper a solution for the development of a microclimate monitoring for Low Voltage / High Voltage switchgear is presented by means of Internet of Things (IoT) platform. This IoT-based real time monitoring system can enable preventive or predictive maintenance to reduce the risk of electrical station malfunctions due to unfavorable environmental conditions. The combination of humidity and dust can lead to unplanned electrical discharges along the isolators inside a low or medium voltage electric table. If no preventive or predictive measures are taken, the situation may deteriorate and lead to significant damage inside the electrical cell and the outside area could be affected as well.

articleTitle: SmartDPO - Template Based, Integrated Flow Document Management System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated flow document management application that is based on blockchain technology and uses the PrivateSky platform. The presented application can be easily adapted to any domain application (metrology, energy). It uses security and confidentiality principles applied with help of PrivateSky technologies and the authors present how these techniques can correct the main shortcomings of existing solutions on the market. The presented app was initially developed based on MVC pattern, and then reconfigured for Action Domain Responder pattern.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing and Placement of Multiple Photovoltaics Considering Electric Vehicles Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Due to the fluctuated generation of Photovoltaic (PV) and stochastic charging and discharging schemes of electric vehicles (EVs), risky operational issues are observed in the medium-voltage distribution systems. Expected issues are excessive energy losses, voltage drop and voltage rise, and disruptions of operational boundaries in power distribution systems. To tackle these issues, we propose an optimization planning model in this paper for optimally allocate PV to accommodate EV charging stations in distribution systems. The proposed planning approach has the ability to determine the best PV locations and sizes to reduce the electrical energy losses in the distribution system, considering voltage and power flow boundaries. Consequently, the allocation problem of PV is created as a double-layer optimization model, which is solved by the gravitational search algorithm. To indicate the effectiveness of the proposed allocation approach of PV, different simulations are performed in the IEEE 69-bus distribution system. The computed results demonstrate that the proposed planning approach can optimally allocate multiple PV units while satisfying the EV charging requirements.

articleTitle: Digital Control and MBPC design for DC Voltage Regulation in a Grid-Connected PV Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The demand and acceptance of photovoltaic (PV) plants have increased steadily in remote agricultural areas of Ecuador, and the design of solar-powered microgrids (MG) provides a solution on these remote sites. The present paper explains the design of a control system used in an MG, based on classical and advanced automatic control techniques, applied to a three-phase inverter connected to a solar array with an irradiance study of the area for its installation. In the first instance, mathematical modeling of the MG inverter is presented. Also, including the design of other electronic components, such as grid filters and a direct current voltage boost converter, to tune two types of controllers, based on digital control and model based predictive control (MBPC), to regulate the alternating voltage given by the MG. A comparative analysis of the performance of both controllers was done, using MATLAB/SIMULINK®, and it was shown that the advanced controller gave a faster response, a lower overvoltage in the MG, and a stabilization of voltage.

articleTitle: Critical Issues in the Design and Operation of Electrical Installations in Hospitals
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The intensive use of electrical equipment in hospital units, especially in conditions of health crisis, causes an increased risk of accidents and fires, primarily due to the undersizing of the power supply and the lack of specific electrical protection elements. The paper aims to highlight all aspects related to the design and use of electrical installations in hospitals, including measures to be taken in accordance with current standards, to avoid the repetition of recent tragedies in treatment centers where fires broke out. Technical details and stages related to the design and safe operation of electrical installations serving medical equipments, considered critical receivers, are provided.

articleTitle: Solving Multimodal Problems Using Genetic Algorithms – A Case Study in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: In multimodal optimization, it is important to obtain all the optima in a single run, for an insightful description of the potential design configurations. Genetic algorithms, as population-based approaches, are very suitable for this purpose. In this paper, the genetic algorithm is designed to work on subpopulations, which use special mechanisms for the insertion of offspring and immigrants. Mainly, the subpopulations are designed to allow speciation, each species being potentially formed around a global optimum. To this end, the insertion mechanism uses a combination of fitness-based and similarity-based insertion techniques, which can help both for preserving the exploration in diverse areas and for improving the accuracy of the solutions. A highly nonlinear problem is considered as a case study – that of finding the propagation constants of a planar dielectric microwave guide. The experimental investigations carried out for different waveguide setups show that using migration with similitude-based insertion of migrants helps achieve accurate locations of all optima, with reasonable computational costs.

articleTitle: Effect of wear process on the security of Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The Fault Tree Analysis is a method which can be used in a preventive or in a corrective manner because it can describe failure mechanisms and also can emphasize the effects of corrective actions performed to remove the causes. The effectiveness of the Fault Tree Analysis depends on the information accuracy about the function that models how the failure occurrences are distributed over time. The objective of this paper is to study how different failure distribution functions of a component are influencing the overall reliability of a system.

articleTitle: Theoretical Considerations, Novel Theory for the Transformers from the National and International Energy System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Theoretical considerations from the past, new visions design for minimizing the dimensions of the distribution transformers in the national and international energy system are exposed. The magnetic field lines, core, coil, material properties are presented. New horizons must be opened to achieve the coveted transformer, the ideal transformer.
